audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Timothy text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact draft reviewed for enslaved/masters, healthy words, contentment, love of money, fight of trust, rich warned, final charge.

verses.restored: As many as are under yoke as enslaved ones, let them consider their own masters worthy of all honor, so that the name of the Divine and the teaching may not be blasphemed.

familiar.text: Let as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed.

modern.text: All who are under the yoke of slavery should regard their masters as fully worthy of honor, so that God’s name and our teaching will not be discredited.

original.text: Ὅσοι εἰσὶν ὑπὸ ζυγὸν δοῦλοι, τοὺς ἰδίους δεσπότας πάσης τιμῆς ἀξίους ἡγείσθωσαν, ἵνα μὴ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἡ διδασκαλία βλασφημῆται.

verses.restored: But those having trusting masters, let them not despise them because they are siblings, but rather serve, because those receiving the good service are trusting and beloved. Teach and appeal these things.

familiar.text: And they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren; but rather do them service, because they are faithful and beloved, partakers of the benefit. These things teach and exhort.

modern.text: Those who have believing masters should not show disrespect because they are brothers, but should serve them all the more, since those receiving their good service are beloved believers. Teach and encourage these principles. Reject False Doctrines

original.text: οἱ δὲ πιστοὺς ἔχοντες δεσπότας μὴ καταφρονείτωσαν, ὅτι ἀδελφοί εἰσιν· ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον δουλευέτωσαν, ὅτι πιστοί εἰσιν καὶ ἀγαπητοὶ οἱ τῆς εὐεργεσίας ἀντιλαμβανόμενοι. Ταῦτα δίδασκε καὶ παρακάλει.

verses.restored: If anyone teaches differently and does not come to healthy words, those of our Lord Jesus Messiah, and to the teaching according to reverence/godliness,

familiar.text: If any man teach otherwise, and consent not to wholesome words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness;

modern.text: If anyone teaches another doctrine and disagrees with the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and with godly teaching,

original.text: εἴ τις ἑτεροδιδασκαλεῖ καὶ μὴ προσέρχεται ὑγιαίνουσι λόγοις, τοῖς τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ τῇ κατʼ εὐσέβειαν διδασκαλίᾳ,

verses.restored: one has been puffed up, understanding nothing, but being diseased around disputes and word-battles, from which come envy, strife, slanders, harmful suspicions,

familiar.text: He is proud, knowing nothing, but doting about questions and strifes of words, whereof cometh envy, strife, railings, evil surmisings,

modern.text: he is conceited and understands nothing. Instead, he has an unhealthy interest in controversies and semantics, out of which come envy, strife, abusive talk, evil suspicions,

original.text: τετύφωται, μηδὲν ἐπιστάμενος, ἀλλὰ νοσῶν περὶ ζητήσεις καὶ λογομαχίας, ἐξ ὧν γίνεται φθόνος, ἔρις, βλασφημίαι, ὑπόνοιαι πονηραί,

verses.restored: constant friction of humans corrupted in mind and deprived of the truth, supposing reverence/godliness to be means of gain.

familiar.text: Perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds, and destitute of the truth, supposing that gain is godliness: from such withdraw thyself.

modern.text: and constant friction between men of depraved mind who are devoid of the truth. These men regard godliness as a means of gain. Godliness with Contentment

original.text: διαπαρατριβαὶ διεφθαρμένων ἀνθρώπων τὸν νοῦν καὶ ἀπεστερημένων τῆς ἀληθείας, νομιζόντων πορισμὸν εἶναι τὴν ⸀εὐσέβειαν.

verses.restored: But reverence/godliness with contentment is great gain.

familiar.text: But godliness with contentment is great gain.

modern.text: Of course, godliness with contentment is great gain.

original.text: ἔστιν δὲ πορισμὸς μέγας ἡ εὐσέβεια μετὰ αὐταρκείας·

verses.restored: For we brought nothing into the world, neither are we able to carry anything out.

familiar.text: For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out.

modern.text: For we brought nothing into the world, so we cannot carry anything out of it.

original.text: οὐδὲν γὰρ εἰσηνέγκαμεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον, ⸀ὅτι οὐδὲ ἐξενεγκεῖν τι δυνάμεθα·

verses.restored: But having food and coverings, with these we will be content.

familiar.text: And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.

modern.text: But if we have food and clothing, we will be content with these.

original.text: ἔχοντες δὲ διατροφὰς καὶ σκεπάσματα, τούτοις ἀρκεσθησόμεθα.

verses.restored: But those wishing to be rich fall into testing and snare and many foolish and harmful desires, which sink humans into ruin and destruction.

familiar.text: But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.

modern.text: Those who want to be rich, however, fall into temptation and become ensnared by many foolish and harmful desires that plunge them into ruin and destruction.

original.text: οἱ δὲ βουλόμενοι πλουτεῖν ἐμπίπτουσιν εἰς πειρασμὸν καὶ παγίδα καὶ ἐπιθυμίας πολλὰς ἀνοήτους καὶ βλαβεράς, αἵτινες βυθίζουσι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους εἰς ὄλεθρον καὶ ἀπώλειαν·

verses.restored: For root of all kinds of harmful things is love of silver/money, which some reaching after were led astray from the trust and pierced themselves around with many pains.

familiar.text: For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.

modern.text: For the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil. By craving it, some have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many sorrows. Fight the Good Fight

original.text: ῥίζα γὰρ πάντων τῶν κακῶν ἐστιν ἡ φιλαργυρία, ἧς τινες ὀρεγόμενοι ἀπεπλανήθησαν ἀπὸ τῆς πίστεως καὶ ἑαυτοὺς περιέπειραν ὀδύναις πολλαῖς.

verses.restored: But you, human of Divine, flee these things; pursue righteousness/justice, reverence/godliness, trust, love, endurance, gentleness.

familiar.text: But thou, O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness.

modern.text: But you, O man of God, flee from these things and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, and gentleness.

original.text: Σὺ δέ, ὦ ἄνθρωπε ⸀θεοῦ, ταῦτα φεῦγε· δίωκε δὲ δικαιοσύνην, εὐσέβειαν, πίστιν, ἀγάπην, ὑπομονήν, ⸀πραϋπαθίαν.

original.text: ἀγωνίζου τὸν καλὸν ἀγῶνα τῆς πίστεως, ἐπιλαβοῦ τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς, εἰς ἣν ἐκλήθης καὶ ὡμολόγησας τὴν καλὴν ὁμολογίαν ἐνώπιον πολλῶν μαρτύρων.

verses.restored: I charge you before the Divine, the One making all things alive, and Messiah Jesus, the One testifying the beautiful/good confession before Pontius Pilate,

original.text: τηρῆσαί σε τὴν ἐντολὴν ἄσπιλον ἀνεπίλημπτον μέχρι τῆς ἐπιφανείας τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,

original.text: ἣν καιροῖς ἰδίοις δείξει ὁ μακάριος καὶ μόνος δυνάστης, ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν βασιλευόντων καὶ κύριος τῶν κυριευόντων,

verses.restored: the only One having deathlessness, dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no human has seen nor is able to see; to whom honor and age-long might. Amen.

familiar.text: Who only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom be honour and power everlasting. Amen.

modern.text: He alone is immortal and dwells in unapproachable light. No one has ever seen Him, nor can anyone see Him. To Him be honor and eternal dominion! Amen. A Charge to the Rich (Proverbs 23:1–5; James 5:1–6)

original.text: ὁ μόνος ἔχων ἀθανασίαν, φῶς οἰκῶν ἀπρόσιτον, ὃν εἶδεν οὐδεὶς ἀνθρώπων οὐδὲ ἰδεῖν δύναται· ᾧ τιμὴ καὶ κράτος αἰώνιον· ἀμήν.

safety_note: 1 Timothy 6:1-2 preserves ancient slavery instructions but must not be used to sanctify slavery or coercive labor. Read with the broader canonical trajectory of release, siblinghood, justice, and the dignity of enslaved people. Wealth warnings should not shame survival needs; they critique greed, status, and trust in riches.
